body:
Priya Raman: Hi Dana, hi Ravi — thanks for making time. I've got Marcus on with me from our SE team. Should we do quick intros and then dive in?

Dana Ortiz: Sure. I'm Dana, I run customer ops here at Fintrust. We handle inbound support for our lending product, roughly forty-two thousand calls a month.

Ravi Chen: And I'm Ravi, director of IT. I own the Salesforce instance and the telephony stack — we're on Genesys today.

Marcus Fields: Great, good to meet you both. Before we go deep, Priya, do you want to frame what we heard from the intro call?

Priya Raman: Yeah, so, the ask was basically — Fintrust wants to deflect tier-one calls, especially payment status and payoff quote lookups. Dana, is that still the primary use case?

Dana Ortiz: That's still it, yes. Those two intents alone are something like sixty percent of our volume. If we could take even half of that off the humans we'd hit our budget target for the year.

Marcus Fields: Understood. Um, on our side voice_agent_v1 handles both of those out of the box — we've got a Salesforce Financial Services Cloud connector that reads account status and payoff balances directly. Ravi, are you on the standard object model or heavily customized?

Ravi Chen: Pretty customized. We've got maybe eighteen custom fields on the Loan__c object and a bunch of validation rules. That's going to be a question mark for us.

Marcus Fields: Okay, that's fair. The connector handles custom fields fine, but validation rules on writes — we'd need to walk through those. Usually a one-week integration sprint covers it.

Dana Ortiz: Can we talk pricing? I want to make sure we're in the ballpark before we spend a lot of cycles.

Priya Raman: Absolutely. Our standard growth-tier pricing is fourteen cents per minute of handled call, with a floor of eight thousand a month. For your volume — you said forty-two thousand calls averaging, what, three minutes?

Dana Ortiz: Closer to four.

Priya Raman: So call it a hundred sixty-eight thousand minutes, that'd land around twenty-three thousand five hundred a month, roughly two-eighty a year on an annual contract.

Dana Ortiz: Yeah, that's — I'll be honest, that's higher than we budgeted. We were modeling around one-eighty a year total. The per-minute rate is the piece that gives me heartburn. Retell quoted us nine cents.

Priya Raman: I hear you. A couple of things — one, we can look at a committed-volume discount that gets the effective rate down to eleven cents. Two, if you're open to a two-year term we can do a further step-down in year two.

Ravi Chen: What about the Salesforce connector — is that separate?

Marcus Fields: The connector's included in the platform fee. Analytics addon is separate, that's an extra fifteen hundred a month if you want the call-outcome dashboards.

Dana Ortiz: Okay, so realistically we're talking, what, two-forty a year with the volume discount?

Priya Raman: With a two-year term, yes, roughly. I can put a formal quote together this week.

Dana Ortiz: Please do. I want to be transparent — the number still has to clear our CFO and she's going to push back. Can you include an ROI model in the quote? Something we can show her that translates minutes deflected into agent hours saved.

Priya Raman: Absolutely. Marcus, can you also include the Genesys handoff diagram? Ravi will want to see how warm transfers work when the bot can't resolve.

Marcus Fields: Will do. Ravi, one question — are you on Genesys Cloud or on-prem?

Ravi Chen: Cloud, thankfully. We migrated last year.

Marcus Fields: Perfect, that's a supported path. SIP trunk handoff, we've done it with three other lenders.

Ravi Chen: What about failover? If your ASR provider goes down mid-call, what happens?

Marcus Fields: We've got a warm-standby transcription provider that kicks in automatically. Failover is sub-second. Callers don't notice.

Ravi Chen: And SOC 2 — we'll need the Type II report before procurement will sign.

Marcus Fields: I'll send it over today. We just refreshed it in June.

Dana Ortiz: One thing I forgot to ask — do we need to bring in our compliance team? We're regulated by CFPB for the servicing side.

Priya Raman: Yes, honestly, sooner rather than later. Our platform has a call-recording consent flow that's built for CFPB and state-level requirements. Better to loop them in before we're deep in contract.

Dana Ortiz: Okay. I'll get Nikhil, our compliance lead, on the next call.

Ravi Chen: One more — do you support multi-tenant call routing? We have two distinct brands under Fintrust umbrella.

Marcus Fields: Yes, you'd set up two separate workspaces under one contract. Shared billing, separate configs.

Ravi Chen: Perfect.

Dana Ortiz: Alright. Let's plan to reconvene in about ten days once we've got the quote and the ROI model. Sound good?

Priya Raman: Ten days works. I'll send a calendar hold for the twenty-fifth.

Dana Ortiz: Thanks folks.

Ravi Chen: One last thing — do you offer a sandbox we can start playing with before contract signature?

Marcus Fields: Yes, we can provision a limited sandbox for two weeks. You'd get five hundred minutes of test traffic.

Ravi Chen: Enough to prototype.

Dana Ortiz: Let's do that in parallel with the quote review.

Priya Raman: Perfect, I'll spin it up tomorrow.

Priya Raman: Thank you both. Really appreciate the time.
